title: Renew Papyrus CLI sessions for at least 24 hours of unattended reporting
description:
Issue filing only, explicitly requested by Ryan. No implementation, login, new credentials, security/configuration changes or deployment is authorized. Parent epic: PPY-7c458d71-3ea8-4c39-8a6c-d2d2ab903df7. Reference: Apricity authorization-code+PKCE login, keychain refresh session and renewal, https://github.com/AnthusAI/Apricity/blob/ffe8a023b0418445aa67893a52ae9e173c366d42/crates/apricity-cli/src/cloud.rs#L206. Preserve existing newsroom authorization and agent attribution; do not conflate CLI auth with hosted procedure execution.

As an authorized reporter I can continue supported CLI work for at least 24 hours without interactive relogin while my session remains unrevoked and publication permissions remain valid.

Feature: Renewable unattended CLI session
  Scenario: Continue past short-lived token expiry
    Given a secure renewable session whose configured lifetime exceeds 24 hours with margin
    When access tokens expire across commands, process restarts and M1 sleep/resume
    Then the CLI silently renews before protected work without opening a browser
    And it uses short-lived tokens rather than a 24-hour access token
  Scenario: Concurrent rotation or temporary failure
    Given two commands share one renewable session
    When token rotation or a timeout, throttling or provider outage occurs
    Then refresh state replacement is atomic and bounded
    And transient errors preserve an otherwise valid session
    And uncertain protected mutations are not blindly replayed
  Scenario: Demonstrate actual elapsed time
    Given an approved end-to-end test with unchanged grants and available services
    When more than 24 real hours elapse after initial login
    Then a supported protected operation succeeds without interactive login
    And timestamped redacted receipts include renewal and restart/sleep evidence

Report configuration inspection, simulated-clock tests and actual elapsed >=24h testing separately. Configured lifetime or a simulated clock does not prove an elapsed 24-hour run; none has passed yet. Exact native-client refresh validity is a reviewed policy choice, not an assumed Apricity production setting. Recoverable expiry and revocation behavior is tracked in the sibling session-security story.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Ryan's cloud CLI extension (2026-10-30): apply the existing renewal/rotation and >=24h acceptance contract to headless Linux, fresh child processes, multiple simultaneous publication bindings, and Windows when supported. Coordinate storage with PPY-109943 and remote approval with PPY-5a3624d4-4f1a-4eee-9bb6-12e575ec3cad. Retain current status/ownership. Distinguish simulated-clock, provider-policy inspection and actual elapsed-time evidence. Retry only safe token operations; never replay an uncertain protected mutation. Removed grants, revocation and absolute expiry fail closed; transient refresh failures preserve valid stored state. No Mac, AWS CLI, or token/code paste is a prerequisite.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Plan (Claude, 2026-10-30).

Mostly built: refresh-token renewal, transient errors preserving the session, and per-site binding. Remaining:
- Run the same contract through each new store (PPY-109943) and through remote-login sessions (PPY-5a3624).
- On invalid_grant, keep deleting the local session, but distinguish revocation or a removed grant (fail closed with recovery guidance) from 429/5xx/network errors (keep the session, bounded retry).
- Never replay an uncertain protected mutation.
- Evidence reported in three separate parts: simulated-clock tests; Cognito client settings inspection (refresh validity, rotation); an actual run of 24 hours or more from a cloud session logged in with --remote, with timestamped redacted receipts across a restart.
